signature: SUBROUTINE ZGERQF( M, N, A, LDA, TAU, WORK, LWORK, INFO )

params.name: M
params.reference: The number of rows of the matrix A. $M \ge 0$.

params.name: N
params.reference: The number of columns of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.

params.name: A
params.reference: On entry, the M-by-N matrix A. On exit, if $m \le n$, the upper triangle of the subarray `A(1:m,n-m+1:n)` contains the M-by-M upper triangular matrix R; if $m \ge n$, the elements on and above the (m-n)-th subdiagonal contain the M-by-N upper trapezoidal matrix R; the remaining elements, with the array `TAU`, represent the unitary matrix Q as a product of min(m,n) elementary reflectors (see Further Details).

params.name: lda
params.reference: The leading dimension of the array A. $\mathrm{LDA} \ge \max (1,M)$.

params.name: TAU
params.reference: The scalar factors of the elementary reflectors (see Further Details).

params.name: WORK
params.reference: On exit, if `INFO = 0`, `WORK(1)` returns the optimal `LWORK`.

params.name: lwork
params.reference:
The dimension of the array `WORK`. $\mathrm{LWORK} \ge 1$, if $\min (M,N) = 0$, and $\mathrm{LWORK} \ge M$, otherwise. For optimum performance $\mathrm{LWORK} \ge M \, \mathrm{NB}$, where NB is the optimal blocksize.

If `LWORK = -1`, then a workspace query is assumed; the routine only calculates the optimal size of the `WORK` array, returns this value as the first entry of the `WORK` array, and no error message related to `LWORK` is issued by XERBLA.

params.name: info
params.reference:
-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value

notes: workspace check for LWORK not reducible to a minimum: LWORK.LE.0 .OR. ( N.GT.0 .AND. LWORK.LT.MAX( 1, M ) )
